record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: In a smooth Euclidean billiard domain with a generic point source of light, after optical reflection at the boundary, does the time-t wave front become dense in the domain as t tends to infinity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, considered as a billiard table: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $\Omega$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting $\partial\Omega$. Fix a point $p \in \Omega$ and consider the family of all unit-speed billiard trajectories emanating from $p$ in every direction; the time-$t$ wave front $W_t(p) \subset \overline{\Omega}$ is the set of points reached at time exactly $t$ along these trajectories (that is, points whose billiard distance from $p$, measured along a trajectory that has undergone the prescribed sequence of reflections, equals $t$). 

Question: For a generic choice of $\Omega$ (smooth Euclidean billiard domain) and generic choice of point source $p \in \Omega$, does the wave front $W_t(p)$ become dense in $\Omega$ as $t \to \infty$? Equivalently, is it true that for every nonempty open set $U \subset \Omega$ there exists $T$ such that $W_t(p) \cap U \neq \emptyset$ for all $t \geq T$?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question for smooth Euclidean billiard domains appears to remain open. A recent (2025) preprint establishes density of wave fronts in special flat settings, namely the flat torus, the square billiard, and certain flat surfaces (Klein bottle, cube), but does not address generic smooth Euclidean billiard tables. No source was found resolving the general case.

status_evidence.title: Density of wave fronts (arXiv:2501.14611)
status_evidence.snippet: Wave fronts on a flat torus become dense; corollaries for square billiard and flat Klein bottle / cube surface geodesic flow.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results establish wave front density only in special flat cases, not for general smooth Euclidean billiards.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Billiards and Geometric Optics
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems including questions on reflected wave fronts in billiard domains.
status_evidence.claim: The wave-front density question is listed among open problems in billiard dynamics.
